markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a small diagnostic that separates earlier-order sensitivity from final-item sensitivity without changing the trained GRU4Rec.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Earlier deletion probes reported substantial padded-versus-unpadded score differences. Changing history length can therefore mix context removal with recurrent execution effects. (2) Anonymous loader rows cannot support user-cluster uncertainty. Explicitly indexed training prefixes permit equal-user aggregation and paired resampling. (3) Strong training-pair margins do not establish held-out ranking quality. The failed prior trial supplies no evidence that its proposed temporal probe worked; its subprocess traceback does not identify the underlying error.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU update gates can preserve state even when saturated [1]. Gate statistics alone cannot establish lost temporal credit. (2) Perturbation conclusions depend on intervention type and region size [2]. Fixed-length controls reduce one source of ambiguity but still introduce distribution shift. (3) Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons [3]. Diagnostic candidate ranks must remain distinct from official validation results.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Observable evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Execution integrity | Repeatability, padding placement, scorer parity | Correct execution does not prove usefulness |
| Temporal sensitivity | Paired, fixed-length order interventions | Sensitivity does not identify current intent |
| Retrieval fidelity | Frozen-candidate and catalog ranks | Training-prefix ranks do not establish generalization |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Fixed-final paired shuffle panel: 4/7/3.** Originality: + combines execution controls and paired uncertainty; − established ablations. Potential: + isolates earlier-order sensitivity cheaply; − in-sample evidence. Difficulty: + existing inference hooks; − tie parity and reproducibility require care [2].
2. **Chunked catalog competition audit: 3/7/4.** Originality: + connects sampled and catalog failures; − standard ranking audit. Potential: + reveals candidate sensitivity; − cannot replace the benchmark. Difficulty: + no retraining; − catalog scoring costs time [3].
3. **Lag-gradient/intervention agreement: 5/6/6.** Originality: + triangulates recurrent credit and perturbations; − familiar attribution methods. Potential: + could guide later recurrent changes; − gradients need not predict finite interventions. Difficulty: + uses one checkpoint; − requires faithful instrumentation and gradients [1,2].

**Selected idea: fixed-final paired shuffle panel.** Freeze one training-prefix target and 99 unique negatives per eligible user. Compare the intact sequence with full shuffling and prefix shuffling that preserves the final item. Both preserve item multiplicities, sequence length and padding placement; their paired difference measures incremental sensitivity to freeing the final position, rather than isolating a causal mechanism.

Average five draws within each user, retain unchanged permutations, and bootstrap complete users within categories. Report rank damage, score margins, changed-draw fractions and tie counts. Use the pinned tie rule; otherwise withhold rank metrics. Preserve all diagnostic interfaces and RNG states. Keep one checkpoint per category and select subsequent training changes only through unchanged macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Implement a reproducible fixed-length paired temporal-sensitivity panel for the supplied GRU4Rec: compare intact histories with full-history shuffles and final-item-fixed prefix shuffles, using the same trained model, target and candidate set.
idea.motivation: Prior deletion diagnostics reported padding-dependent score changes, while sampled training margins supplied no held-out improvement evidence. Fixed-length shuffling preserves padding placement and item multiplicities, allowing a narrower investigation of arrangement sensitivity. At early research progress, this is more feasible than recurrent instrumentation and makes no unsupported claims about compatibility, mood or intent.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use the actual view.model and existing item_emb, log2feats and predict_score interfaces. Construct explicitly user-indexed cases from user_train, selecting at most 200 eligible users per category deterministically and one training-prefix target per user with at least five retained interactions. Freeze target plus 99 unique real-item negatives excluding the user's complete training history and target; report insufficient candidate pools rather than relaxing uniqueness. These are diagnostic cases, not host validation cases. Preserve external sequence width, padding placement and duplicate multiplicities. Gather the maximum nonzero position, never count minus one. Verify finite outputs, repeated-call consistency and batch-order independence; measure exported-predictor parity only if its callable is available, otherwise report unavailable. Do not silently alter recurrence or assume padding invariance. Use five draws per intervention with local SeedSequence([42, stable_user_index, intervention_id]) generators and save cases, candidates, permutations and configuration beneath the trial directory. Include identity and duplicate-induced unchanged draws in primary estimates, with changed-draw summaries separately labeled. Use the pinned evaluator's exact tie convention when available; otherwise return rank and HR fields null with a reason while retaining score diagnostics. Average draws within users and users equally; bootstrap complete paired user records with 2,000 seed-42 replicates when at least 30 complete users exist. Report intervals conditional on checkpoints, candidates and realized permutations, excluding training-seed uncertainty. A category-local probe returns macro fields null; aggregate equally only when all four categories are available. Restore model mode and Python, NumPy, Torch and CUDA RNG states in finally. Preserve existing diagnostics and the five-per-category full-catalog unseen-item recommendation workflow. Do not use unavailable metadata or infer simulator traits. No architecture or predictor change is proposed. Preserve all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and one independently trained checkpoint per category. No improvement or successful execution is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved_state = capture_model_mode_and_all_rng_states()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                existing = run_existing_family_specific_diagnostics(train_loader)
                checks = audit_repeatability_shapes_finiteness_and_batch_order(self.view)
                if not checks.pass_required_checks:
                    return merge_with_unavailable_temporal_metrics(existing, checks)
                cases = build_deterministic_user_indexed_training_prefixes(
                    self.view.user_train, max_users=200, minimum_history=5,
                    unique_negatives=99, seed=42)
                records = []
                for stable_index, case in enumerate(cases):
                    positions = nonzero_positions(case.sequence)
                    candidates = case.frozen_candidates
                    def score(sequence):
                        states = self.view.log2feats(sequence)
                        features = states[:, maximum_nonzero_position(sequence), :]
                        return self.view.predict_score(features, candidates)
                    original = score(case.sequence)
                    record = initialize_user_record(case, original)
                    for intervention_id, mode in enumerate(['full', 'fixed_final']):
                        rng = local_seed_sequence_rng(42, stable_index, intervention_id)
                        movable = positions if mode == 'full' else positions[:-1]
                        for draw in range(5):
                            permutation = rng.permutation(len(movable))
                            altered = copy(case.sequence)
                            altered[movable] = case.sequence[movable[permutation]]
                            perturbed = score(altered)
                            record.append(paired_score_and_rank_statistics(
                                original, perturbed, candidates,
                                exact_host_tie_rule_or_none,
                                changed=not_equal(altered, case.sequence),
                                permutation=permutation))
                    records.append(record)
                save_trial_local_cases_and_interventions(records)
                summary = average_draws_then_users(records)
                summary.update(paired_user_bootstrap_if_eligible(records, 2000, 42))
                summary['macro'] = None
                return merge_metrics_and_definitions(existing, checks, summary)
        finally:
            restore_model_mode_and_all_rng_states(saved_state)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return interpretation_prompt_with_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        limits=['training-prefix sensitivity', 'perturbation distribution shift',
                'fixed candidate/checkpoint conditioning',
                'no causal intent or validation-improvement inference'])

originality.positive: Combines final-item controls, fixed-length interventions, explicit execution checks and paired user aggregation in a focused GRU4Rec diagnostic.
originality.negative: Shuffling, paired comparisons and user bootstrap intervals are established methods; the contribution is incremental integration.

future_potential.positive: Offers inexpensive evidence for choosing subsequent experiments on earlier-order learning versus final-item dependence while preserving the single-model constraint.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix sensitivity under artificial permutations cannot establish generalization, harmful shortcuts or current user intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing feature and scoring interfaces without retraining, modifying GRU internals or changing the predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact tie-rule parity, deterministic candidate construction, paired aggregation and RNG restoration require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Improving the Gating Mechanism of Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Studies recurrent gating and motivates distinguishing state preservation from ease of learning.
Supports treating gate saturation as incomplete evidence about temporal credit.
limitations: Does not validate the supplied GRU4Rec checkpoint or establish recommendation improvements.
Gate observations alone omit the full recurrent derivative and target-ranking effects.

related_work.title: [2] Time-series perturbation study (2025), supplied search result
contributions: The supplied search summary reports sensitivity of evaluation conclusions to perturbation method and region size.
Motivates using explicit intervention controls and reporting the scope of each estimand.
limitations: General time-series methodology does not directly establish mechanisms in GRU4Rec.
Fixed-length shuffling still creates distribution shift and can change several dependencies simultaneously.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation and alter model comparisons.
Motivates separating fixed-candidate sensitivity diagnostics from catalog retrieval and official benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not determine the performance of this checkpoint or invalidate the task's pinned selection metric.
A catalog audit on training prefixes remains conditional diagnostic evidence rather than held-out evaluation.
